info.title: TMS Requisition API
info.summary: Vehicle requisition module — list, create, view, edit and cancel.
info.description:
Reconstructed from the Postman collection `TMS Requisition API`
(`_postman_id: 1463e366-27a1-4d3f-a15b-e8af1b665fdc`).

## Accuracy notice — read before implementing

The source collection contains **no saved response examples**. Every
response body below is therefore inferred from two things only:

1. The collection's test scripts (`body.data.token`, `body.data.id`).
2. The prose in each request's `description` field.

Any schema, field or status code carrying `x-status: inferred` is an
**open question for the backend team**, not an agreed contract. Fields
marked `x-status: confirmed` were observed directly in the collection.

Treat this document as a review artifact: send it to the API owner,
get the inferred parts either confirmed or corrected, then bump the
version to `1.0.0` and delete this notice.

## Domain invariant

Both mutating operations (`PUT /requisitions/{id}` and
`POST /requisitions/{id}/cancel`) are gated by the same two conditions:

    status == "Pending"   AND   actor == original creator

Neither is a client-side-only check. A requisition can leave `Pending`
at any moment because an approver acted on it, so a client holding a
stale list will get a `409` on an action its UI still shows as legal.
Design for that path explicitly.

contact.name: Backend team — TMS
x-open-questions: `X-Requisition-Source` is sent BOTH as an HTTP header and as a body field on create. Which one does the server actually read? Is either required? This spec models the header as authoritative and omits the body duplicate — confirm before relying on it.

`pick_up_date_time` uses `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` with no timezone offset. Which zone does the server interpret it in? Assumed Asia/Dhaka (UTC+06:00) — must be confirmed, a one-hour drift misdispatches a driver.

The collection declares an unused variable `logistic_requisition_id`, implying a second requisition type (logistic vehicle?) with its own create/update payload. Is there a `req_type` beyond `passenger_vehicle`, and does it share these endpoints?
No error envelope is documented anywhere. Please supply one sample each of 401, 403, 409 and 422 so the client error mapper can be written against real shapes.
What is the complete `status` vocabulary and the legal transitions between values? Only `Pending` and a cancelled state are mentioned.
Does the list response wrap results in pagination metadata, and if so what is the envelope? Assumed Laravel-style — confirm.
Do tokens expire, and is there a refresh or logout endpoint?

servers.description: Mirrors the collection's `base_url` variable. The collection default is cleartext HTTP on localhost, which is fine locally but will be blocked by Android's default network security config on API 28+. Staging and production must be HTTPS.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Session establishment. The API resolves the acting user from the token.

post.summary: Exchange credentials for a bearer token
post.description:
Returns a token that every other operation sends as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The API identifies the acting user
from this token — no user id is passed on any other request.

get.summary: Get the account behind the current token
get.description: Returns the authenticated user's account info, resolved from the bearer token. Useful as a cheap token-validity probe on app start.
Lists requisitions created by the authenticated user, optionally filtered by a date range. Scoping is implicit — there is no user/owner query parameter.

post.description: Creates a requisition owned by the authenticated user. The new resource starts in `Pending`, which is the only status from which it can later be edited or cancelled.

get.description: Returns full detail — assigned driver and vehicle, plus the audit log — for a single requisition. Ownership is enforced: a caller who is not the creator receives `403`, not `404`.

put.summary: Update a requisition (Pending only, creator only)
put.description:
Full replacement of the mutable fields.

Three constraints, all server-enforced:

- `req_type` **must match the requisition's existing type exactly**.
  This endpoint cannot convert a requisition from one type to
  another; sending a different value is an error, not a conversion.
- The requisition's status must still be `Pending`.
- The caller must be the original creator.

post.summary: Cancel a requisition (Pending only, creator only)
post.description: Transitions a `Pending` requisition to cancelled. Takes no body. Returns `409` if the requisition has already been cancelled or has otherwise moved out of `Pending` — which is the expected outcome when a client acts on a stale list, so treat it as a normal UI path rather than an unexpected failure.

bearerAuth.description: Token obtained from `POST /login`. Expiry and refresh semantics are undocumented — see `info.contact.x-open-questions`.

FromDate.name: fdate
FromDate.description: Inclusive start of the filter range. Optional — the server defaults to one month ago. Note this is a bare date, whereas `pick_up_date_time` in request bodies is a date-time; the two formats are not interchangeable.

ToDate.name: tdate
ToDate.description: Inclusive end of the filter range. Optional — the server defaults to today.

RequisitionSource.name: X-Requisition-Source
RequisitionSource.description: Identifies the client application originating the requisition. The collection also sends an identically-named field inside the request body; this spec treats the header as authoritative and omits the body copy. Confirm with the backend team before relying on either — see `info.contact.x-open-questions`.

RequisitionId.description: Type is inferred. The Postman test script assigns `body.data.id` straight into a collection variable without coercion, so it could be an integer or a string. Confirm before choosing a client-side type — parsing an id as `Int` that later becomes a UUID is a breaking change.

user_name.description: An email address in the observed sample, though the field is not named `email` — confirm whether other identifier formats are accepted.

LoginRequest.x-security-note: The source collection hard-codes a real corporate address and the password `123456` in this request body. Rotate that credential and move secrets into a Postman environment with secret-typed variables.

token.description: Bearer token for all subsequent requests.

LoginResponse.description: Only the `data.token` path is confirmed — the test script reads exactly that. Sibling fields such as expiry or the user object may also be present.

data.description: Field set entirely unknown — the collection never inspects this response. Request a sample payload.

ReqType.description: Only `passenger_vehicle` is observed. The collection's unused `logistic_requisition_id` variable suggests at least one further type exists; it is deliberately NOT listed here because that would assert something unverified. Confirm the full vocabulary.

RequisitionFor.description: Free-text on the wire, but behaves as a closed vocabulary. Only `Own User` observed — capitalisation appears load-bearing.

RequisitionForUser.description: Only `Internal User` observed. An `External User` counterpart is plausible but unverified.

UsedType.description: Journey shape. Two values observed. Note the literal ampersand and spacing in `Pickup & Drop` — it is an exact-match string, so it must be URL-encoded in query contexts and never reconstructed from parts. A `Pickup`-only counterpart is plausible but unverified.

RequisitionStatus.description: Only `Pending` is named in the collection, plus an unnamed cancelled state. The real vocabulary and its transitions are unknown — this is the single most important gap, because the entire edit/cancel permission model hangs off it.

LocalDateTime.description: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` — a space separator and no timezone offset, so this is NOT RFC 3339 and `format: date-time` would be wrong. Assumed to be Asia/Dhaka (UTC+06:00) wall-clock time; pin that explicitly client-side rather than letting the device locale decide.

RequisitionWriteRequest.description: Shared body for create and update. Update is a full replacement, and on update `req_type` must equal the requisition's existing type. Required-vs-optional below is inferred from the sample payloads — every field appears in both samples, so the split is a guess. Ask which fields the server actually validates as required.

customer_name.description: Present in both samples. Whether it is required, and whether it is conditional on `requisition_for_user` being external, is unknown.

pickup_location.description: Free-text address, not a coordinate pair. If this module ever needs to feed dispatch or ETA logic it will need geocoding on top — worth raising early.

drop_location.description: Likely conditional on `used_type` — a pickup-only journey plausibly has no drop. Confirm the conditional-required rule.

no_of_person.description: Passenger count. Upper bound, if any, is unknown.

remarks.description: Free-text note for the fleet team.

Requisition.description: Read model. Only `id` is confirmed; the rest is projected from the write model plus the endpoint descriptions, which mention status, driver, vehicle and an audit log. Request a real sample before writing client models against this.

driver.description: Populated once a driver is assigned. Field set unknown.

vehicle.description: Populated once a vehicle is assigned. Field set unknown.

audit_log.description: Mentioned in the detail endpoint description. Entry shape unknown — presumably actor, action and timestamp.

RequisitionDetailResponse.description: The `data` envelope is confirmed for create (the test script reads `body.data.id`) and assumed identical for view, update and cancel.

RequisitionListResponse.description: Hypothesis: the backend is Laravel and this is a standard paginated resource collection — the `per_page` parameter name, the `data` envelope and the 422 validation convention all point that way. The collection never inspects this response, so nothing here is verified.

PaginationMeta.description: Shape unverified. Do not build a paging component against this until confirmed.

ErrorResponse.description: No error payload appears anywhere in the collection. This is a placeholder following the common Laravel convention. It is the highest-value thing to get confirmed, because the client cannot distinguish recoverable from fatal errors without it.

errors.description: Field-keyed validation messages, if the convention holds.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed or expired bearer token. Client action: clear the stored session and route to login.

NotTheCreator.description: The caller is authenticated but is not the requisition's creator. Explicitly documented for the detail endpoint and assumed to apply to update and cancel too. Client action: this is terminal — do not retry, and surface it as a permission message rather than a generic failure.

NotFound.description: No requisition with that id. Not documented in the collection.

NotPending.description: The requisition is no longer `Pending`, so it can be neither edited nor cancelled. Documented for cancel; assumed to apply to update. Client action: this usually means the local copy is stale — refetch the requisition and re-render available actions rather than showing a generic error.

ValidationFailed.description: Request body or query parameters failed validation. Client action: map `errors` onto the offending form fields.
